purpose: What a finished module graph must contain, as distinct from what a shard may say. The v3 contract is a vocabulary -- which node kinds and relation kinds exist, how ids are spelled, what shape a record takes. It says nothing about whether the assembled graph can be played. This says that.
why_two_layers: Modules differ too much for counts to be law: a one-scene handout has no branches, and a campaign has forty. So the invariants are structural -- properties any playable graph has whatever its size -- and everything that varies by book is measured and reported, never thresholded.
accounting_law: An invariant asks that something be accounted for, not that a particular thing exist. The account has to be a statement about the thing itself -- an explicit empty entry_scene_ids says the book names no entrance -- and never a coverage status: a merged graph says `partial` about nearly every domain, so reading an account out of coverage leaves a door that is always open.

invariants.asks: Every relation's endpoints are nodes the graph defines.
invariants.why: A relation to a node that does not exist is an exit the Keeper cannot take.

invariants.asks: The scene graph is one piece: every scene is joined to every other by some chain of exits.
invariants.why: A separate piece is a part of the book the Keeper has no move into. Measured on a real build: twenty-six scenes in eight pieces, the largest holding nine. Rooting reachability at 'scenes nothing leads into' hides this exactly, because each piece then has a root of its own.

invariants.asks: Once an entrance is declared, every scene is reachable from it by exit relations.
invariants.why: Direction matters only after somebody says where play starts.

invariants.asks: The graph names at least one entry scene, or says the book names none with an explicit empty entry_scene_ids.
invariants.why: Without an entrance the Keeper has nowhere to open, and the campaign projection has no first scene to activate.

invariants.asks: The graph names at least one ending, or says the book states none with an explicit empty ending_scene_ids.
invariants.why: A module that cannot end cannot be finished. Open-ended modules exist; unstated endings are the thing being caught.

invariants.asks: Every clue supports at least one conclusion.
invariants.why: A clue that answers no question never reaches the runtime: the belief state advances conclusions, and a clue outside that chain is scenery.

invariants.asks: Every conclusion is supported by at least one clue.
invariants.why: A conclusion players have no route to is an answer with no question attached to it.

invariants.asks: Every clue is discoverable at at least one scene.
invariants.why: A clue in no scene cannot be found, whatever it supports.

invariants.asks: Every npc and creature is present-in at least one scene.
invariants.why: An actor no scene contains can never be met.

invariants.asks: Every node cites at least one evidence span that names a page.
invariants.why: An unprovable node is worse than a missing one; this is what makes the graph auditable against the book.

measures.asks: How many relations the projection turns into an exit.
Connected pieces of the scene graph; one is whole.
Scenes with more than one outgoing exit.
Share of the module's evidence spans some node or claim cites.
